rv.q: In Brigid Larmour’s finely etched production, irritable passions ferment beneath the frowsty knits and beads.
This is a wonderful revival of a marvellous play.
The Old Ladies really is a creaky old piece of theatre.
Ms Thaw seems slightly miscast and too young to play the sinister and crotchety battle-axe.

cn.t: This 1935 thriller feels dated and tame to some, but its atmospheric portrayal of lonely, impoverished elderly women resonates with contemporary relevance, earning mixed-to-positive reviews for its compassionate period piece qualities.
